Key Activities: Plans and conducts the analysis of statistical program data; writes and edits analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
Conducts analysis of socio-economic trends and developments to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Provides feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures following data analysis and makes recommendations for improvements to established survey methods and activities.
Provides advisory and consultative services as well as subject matter advice to data users within and outside STC.
Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees in various roles such as Project Manager, Task manager and Task Force Leader.
Leads project teams involved in the conduct of subject matter studies/reviews.

1. DECISION MAKING: Investigates client requirements for statistical information, determines the nature and scope of studies, as well as the sources of information, methods and approaches to be used. Modifies existing techniques or develops new methods of collecting, processing, editing, compiling and presenting statistical data.

Assesses the requirement to conduct research into socio-economic trends and developments, evaluates feasibility studies and project proposals submitted by stakeholders and makes recommendations to senior management.

Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.
Interprets preliminary results, reviews study format and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary.

Develops proposals for futher study and recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection or production systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection or statistical production activities.
Determines the need for and prepares specifications and guidelines for the contracting of work to internal service areas, outside agencies and contractors.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Supervises project teams involved in the conduct of unique, complex and/or non-recurring subject matter studies/reviews and/or leads project teams for special projects/studies. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, participates in the recruitment of staff, provides input to employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going studies and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated.
3. COMMUNICATION: Provides subject-matter expertise and advice to all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, regarding potential development areas or to identify and resolve processing and marketing issues. As Subject Matter Specialist, the studies, analyses, forecasts and advice are usually accepted by senior management without substantial changes, and are the first stage in formulating departmental policy or action on opportunities or problems in this sector.

Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources, timeframes and costs with service providers (e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.

Attends meetings with senior officials to interpret or explain study results and recommendations. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the collection and compilation of data and the quality of outputs.
Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify current developments or to explain the results of studies.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of expertise.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: Knowledge of economic/ sociology principles and practices as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of the area. This is necessary to initiate and conduct studies/projects to improve existing concepts or develop new approaches to extend the application of divisional statistics, and to analyze, review and present survey findings. This knowledge is also required to provide subject-matter expertise, advice and consultative services to users, within and outside STC, as well as to provide related advice to other professionals.

Knowledge of statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data.
Management skills and knowledge of the theories and principles of general and project management to lead a multi-disciplinary project team.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the conduct and management of studies/reviews.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage subject matter studies/reviews. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.

Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements. Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on survey results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Interprets study results, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Reviews and modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Some studies may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data have been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.

Reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs, reviews and resolves technical and conceptual problems referred by staff or project team members.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user requirements for statistical information and to translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request. Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.
